verdicts.proposal_name: Procyclical credit supply: zeta(x), with tau and kappa_b recalibrated
verdicts.critique:
Two independent, verified, fatal errors.

(1) THE V-SHAPE DOES NOT EXIST. The proposal's entire 'why FF/FM cannot' argument rests on G_i = P_up - P_down being a symmetric, envelope-theorem-zero function of (b_i - b*). I loaded the shipped solfiles and computed G/P_down directly. On the support the simulation actually visits (b in [0, 0.32]; b_refin_0 takes only the three values {0.2105, 0.2632, 0.3158} over the ENTIRE 80,000-point grid), G/P is MONOTONE DECREASING and nearly exactly linear in b: at the median (z,x) it runs 0.00826, 0.00651, 0.00458, 0.00251, 0.00045, -0.00126, -0.00197 across b = 0 to 0.316. Linear R^2 of G/P on b over that range: mean 0.930, median 0.988 (across 400 (z,x) slices). Over the full grid it is 0.714 and the curve is a monotone convex RIGHT arm (G/P = 0.489 at b=1 vs 0.0083 at b=0, a 59x asymmetry). The proposal's own numerical evidence -- 'linear R^2 of exp(-c|u|) is 0.000' -- is a property of an object this model does not contain.

The reason is structural and the proposal has the economics backwards: eta=1 is a FORCED refinancing, not an option. GS21.m line ~253 sets prof0_up = pi_Rmat + ((1-kappa_b)*Q_0(b') - Q_0(b)), so at b'=b the firm pays kappa_b*Q_0 for nothing. Hence P_up >= P_down - kappa_b*Q_0, and the observed minimum G/P = -0.00197 at b=0.316 equals exactly -kappa_b*Q_0/P_down = -0.004*95.8/194.5. G is not an option value, it is not bounded below by zero, and it has no vertex. Over the visited support the dominant force is 'low-leverage firms want to lever up to capture the tax shield' -- a monotone, linear-in-book_lev premium, which is precisely what Fama-MacBeth spans best.

(2) THE AMPLITUDE IS OVERSTATED BY ~20x AND EXCEEDS A HARD UPPER BOUND. The proposal asserts beta_credit = (G/P)*theta_zeta = 0.46*(G/P), justified by 'the one-period factor zeta*theta ~ 0.0046 is multiplied by the ~100-month duration ... so the duration and the small zeta cancel to O(1).' That double-counts. Correctly: dV/dzeta = sum_s E[M_{t,t+s} G_{t+s}] ~ G*D with D = 1/(1-delta*rho_G) ~ 35-55; the innovation in zeta is zeta*theta*sqrt(1-rho_x^2) = 0.01*0.46*0.183 = 8.4e-4; and the PV-weighted persistence factor is avg(rho_x^s) under duration-D weights ~ 0.6, NOT D. Product: dlogP/d(1sd x) from the credit channel = 35 * 0.01 * 0.46 * 0.183 * 0.63 * (G/P) = 0.019*(G/P). That is 24x below the claimed 0.46*(G/P). Worse, there is a hard ceiling: zeta*D <= zeta/(r + zeta + p_invest) = 0.01/(0.0083+0.01+0.0198) = 0.26 and cannot exceed 1 even as zeta grows (because raising zeta shrinks G by keeping b near b*), so beta_credit <= 0.46*0.183*0.63*(G/P) = 0.053*(G/P). The claimed coefficient violates this bound by 9x. With sd(G/P) = 0.0024 the credit loading has cross-sectional sd 4.6e-5 against the existing systematic loading sd of ~0.00133 -- 3.5%, contributing ~0.1% of var(mu), not the claimed 86%. Even the hoped-for 3x recalibration of tau/kappa_b leaves it at ~1% of var(mu).

(3) INTERNAL CONSISTENCY. You cannot make zeta state-dependent when the baseline zeta is already inconsistent between the two halves of the code: GS21.m line 35 sets xi = 0.03/3*3 = 0.03, config.py line 296 sets GS21_ZETA = 0.03/3 = 0.01. The shipped value function was solved at a refinancing rate 3x the one the simulation and sdf_compute_gs21.py use. Any zeta(x) built on top of this inherits the error.

(4) IDENTITY. Procyclical credit supply is defensible economics with real empirical support (I do not dispute the citations). But it is not in Gomes-Schmid, it makes the arrival rate of the model's defining friction an exogenous priced process, and combined with a tau that must be raised 3x and a kappa_b raised 5x it is a recalibration of the model, not a repair of it.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: FF and FM capture it almost entirely, and my numbers say so directly. The object is 93-99% linear in book_lev on the visited support, so FM's X(X'X)^{-1} portfolios -- which are exactly the linear characteristic-managed portfolios -- span it. FF is not blind either: the proposal argues a 2x3 sort on a symmetric loading nets to zero, but G is monotone in b, so a high-minus-low mkt_lev/book_lev tercile sort captures it with the right sign and near-full efficiency. And the gap would be tiny regardless: at the correct beta_credit ~ 0.02*(G/P), the new priced direction is ~0.1% of the variance of expected returns and would be invisible against the existing rank-1 x-factor. Even granting the proposal's own target of sd(G/P) = 0.007, you get ~1% of var(mu) in a direction that is 93% linear -- so the residual non-linear, unspanned content is ~0.07% of var(mu). The measured population span numbers (linear-6 at 0.871 of max SR^2) would move by less than one part in a thousand. There is no plausible parameterization inside the calibration that rescues this: to make the credit loading rival the existing one you need sd(G/P) ~ 0.06, i.e. the refinancing wedge worth 6% of equity value in cross-sectional dispersion, which is 25x the current value and requires the model to be a different model.
verdicts.salvage: Keep only the diagnostic content: the finding that GS21's refinancing option is economically trivial (sd(G/P) = 0.0024) and that eta=1 is a forced, costly refinancing rather than an option is worth reporting as a limitation of the model. If a credit channel is still wanted, the defensible version is a STATE-DEPENDENT PRICE OF RISK, gamma_x(x) in GS21.m's Mmat (line 138), rather than a state-dependent zeta: it costs no grid dimension, no free amplitude, is squarely inside the Epstein-Zin/long-run-risk lineage the model already declares (GS21.m lines 14-16), and it makes the cross-sectional premium of leverage move with the macro state -- which is the char-by-macro interaction the estimator can actually see. Be honest that it leaves the conditional covariance rank at 1. Separately, before ANY of this: reconcile xi = 0.03 (GS21.m) with GS21_ZETA = 0.01 (config.py:296) and verify GS21.m reproduces the shipped solfiles.

verdicts.proposal_name: Repair mkt_lev and add five characteristics the model already generates
verdicts.critique:
The mkt_lev repair is a genuine, unambiguous bug fix and should ship regardless of everything else. panel_functions_gs21.py:278 computes mkt_lev = book_lev * bm = b/P_ex, where b is the monthly COUPON per unit capital, not the value of debt. I verified the correct object from the shipped solfiles: at the median (z,x), Q_0/(Q_0+P_down) runs 0.000, 0.057, 0.113, 0.169, 0.225, 0.278, 0.330 across bgrid = 0 to 0.316, and b_refin_0 = 0.316 at the center, so the model's firms sit at 33% market leverage -- exactly GS21's calibration target. The prior diagnosis's headline 'GS21 firms are effectively all-equity (max 1% market leverage)' is an artifact of the broken characteristic, and it has been used to justify Proposals 5 and 6. Correcting it materially weakens the case for widening bmax. Q_0 is already an in-scope interpolator (sdf_compute_gs21.py:41, imported by panel_functions_gs21.py:15), so the fix is two lines with no re-solve.

Three of the five additions should be dropped or gated.

cfvol IS ACTIVELY HARMFUL IN THE BASELINE, and the proposal gets its sign backwards. It argues cfvol is valuable because it is a NOISY proxy for the type. But in the baseline there are no types: sigma_z is a single scalar (config.py:289) common to every firm, and roe_t = (1-tau)exp(x_{t-1}+z_{t-1}) - delta with x cross-sectionally constant. So the population cash-flow volatility is IDENTICAL across firms and a 36-month rolling std is PURE cross-sectional sampling noise with no signal at all. That is not 'the noisy proxy AIPT requires'; it is a null characteristic. The BGN diagnosis already documented what a null char does in this pipeline: agr (91% ties) enters 1 of 6 FM regressors additively but ALL 3600 RFF features multiplicatively, raising the feature PCs needed for 99% of variance from 59 to 95. cfvol would do the same to GS21, handicapping DKKM specifically. Gate it strictly on Proposal 4 landing with real type heterogeneity.

dd is a constant. z_cut_down.csv contains a single unique value, -0.146826069677159, equal to zgrid.min() at every one of the 400 (x,b) points -- I verified this. So dd = (z - const)/sd is an affine transform of z, i.e. a duplicate of rank-standardized roe. It adds a perfectly collinear column that degrades FM's already-poorly-conditioned pinvh design (fama_functions.fama_macbeth regresses on RAW unstandardized chars) while adding a redundant RFF input. Drop until Proposal 5 makes the boundary interior.

ivest is fine and strictly better than agr. I confirm the degeneracy: i_cut_down over the grid has min 1.29, mean 39.57, max 122.60 against imax = 2000, so P(invest) is 0.06%-6.1% per month with mean 1.98%.

One caveat the proposal misses: the repaired mkt_lev is a smooth monotone function of (b, P_ex), and the panel already carries book_lev and bm = 1/P_ex. So the repaired char is close to being in the span of two chars FM would already have, and it will not by itself add span.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: It will not, and the proposal concedes this. Every added characteristic is handed to FM linearly and to FF as an extra sort. The effective-rank argument (20.7 at L=6 to 38.5 at L=10) is real but it is a statement about the estimator's dictionary, not about the truth: the pipeline audit already established that the RFF map's effective rank is 16-21 while the DKKM AIPT regime needs ~500, so doubling 20 to 38 does not change the regime. Meanwhile each added char raises FF/FM's plug-in Sharpe loss from ~2K/T = 3.9% (K=7) to ~6.1% (K=11), which is a mechanical handicap to the linear methods that a referee will correctly call out as manufacturing the gap by degrading the benchmark rather than improving the model. The honest expected effect on DKKM/FM is zero to slightly negative.
verdicts.salvage: Ship exactly two items now, framed as bug fixes rather than as a proposal: (a) mkt_lev = Q_0/(Q_0 + mve) using the already-loaded Q_0 interpolator; (b) ivest as a 12-month rolling investment rate replacing or supplementing the degenerate agr, together with the note that FF's cma sort on agr is a 92/0/8 split. Keep book_lev as a char. Hold cfvol until Proposal 4 supplies genuine sigma heterogeneity, and hold dd until the default boundary is interior. Report the linear methods at BOTH char sets so the K-inflation handicap is visible.

verdicts.proposal_name: Restore sigma_z to the paper calibration, raise rho_z, repair the solve-vs-simulation mismatches
verdicts.critique:
This proposal contains the single most important item in the entire set, but it buries it under a calibration change that is far more contestable.

THE MISMATCH IS REAL, EXACT, AND FATAL TO THE CURRENT BASELINE. I verified it to six decimals from the shipped grids. GS21.m line 25 uses sigma_z = 0.16*sqrt((1-0.9^(2/3))/(1-0.9^2)); config.py:289 uses the exponent 3/2 and a 0.1 factor. Solving each: the 2/3 form times 0.1 gives sigma_z = 0.0095599, whose 4-sd stationary band is 0.14682607 -- and zgrid.max() in the shipped solfile is 0.146826069677159, an exact match. The 3/2 form gives 0.014034, band 0.21555, no match. Same for x: the 2/3 form gives sigma_x = 0.0070463, band 0.15372303; xgrid.max() = 0.153723027652884, exact match. THEREFORE: the shipped value function was solved for a process with sigma_z 1.468x and sigma_x 1.484x SMALLER than the one panel_functions_gs21.py:40-41 simulates and than the one sdf_compute_gs21.py:91-92 integrates over. Consequences: (i) P_up/P_down/i_cut/b_refin are not optimal policies for the simulated economy; (ii) the state wanders to +/-2.7 solve-sd and is linearly extrapolated off-grid because every interpolator sets fill_value=None (sdf_compute_gs21.py:61-74); (iii) most damaging, erets, rp, cond_var and max_sr -- the objects the Sharpe metric scores every method against -- are not the true conditional moments of ANY internally consistent model. The whole GS21 exercise is currently uninterpretable, and this is a prerequisite, not a proposal.

TWO FURTHER MISMATCHES, both confirmed by direct read. (a) GS21.m line 27 sets r = 0.1/12 = 0.0083333 inside Mmat, so the pricing kernel discounts at 10%/yr; config.py:299 sets GS21_R = 0.074830/12 = 0.0062358, used in panel_functions_gs21.py:296 (df.ret -= exp(r)-1) and sdf_compute_gs21.py (ER[0,0] = exp(2r), ER[0,1:] = (eret+1)*exp(r)). Every 'true' conditional risk premium therefore carries a spurious +0.0021/month = +2.5%/yr level. Against a measured cross-sectional MEAN rp of 0.35-1.33%/month, that wedge is a large fraction -- possibly most -- of the aggregate premium, and it inflates the market leg of max_sr. (b) GS21.m line 124 sets pi_Rmat = (exp(x+z) - delta) - (1-tau)*b (operating profit untaxed), while panel_functions_gs21.py:113-118 uses (1-tau)*exp(x+z) - delta - (1-tau)*b. Confirmed.

WHERE THE PROPOSAL OVERREACHES. rho_z = 0.985 is not a repair, it is a new calibration choice that GS21 never made, and it is the item that forces the 15x z-grid widening and the memory blow-up the proposal itself flags. The FHS 0.8-annual-TFP and FF 0.85-annual-profitability citations are about plant TFP and firm profitability, not about the persistence of the specific z that enters this model's cash flow, and GS21's own 0.9-annual is inside the range those studies support. Raising it is defensible but it is a discretionary parameter change that the paper would have to defend, and it is separable from the bug fixes. Ship the two separately.

SECOND OVERREACH: the proposal's channel (iii), 'it fixes the SNR by raising idiosyncratic volatility 3-5x,' is quantitatively wrong -- see my critique of Proposal 4. GS21's idiosyncratic return variance is ~95% the investment lottery, not the z process. Restoring sigma_z 10x would move the z-channel's contribution to idio variance from 9.4e-6 to 9.4e-4, so it WOULD become dominant -- but only under the full 10x restoration to the paper value (0.0956), not under the milder fixes, and the proposal does not identify the competing channel it is fighting.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: The mismatch repairs will not produce a gap; they will make the existing numbers MEAN something, which may move them in either direction. Fixing r alone strips ~2.5%/yr of spurious premium and will lower every reported Sharpe and max_sr. Fixing the sigma exponents SHRINKS the simulated shocks by ~1.47x, further compressing an already-degenerate cross-section. So the honest prediction for the repair package is that GS21 gets WORSE-looking, not better. On the rho_z/sigma_z restoration itself, the proposal is admirably candid that FM harvests 76-92% of a monotone heteroskedasticity channel; I would go further, because the interaction it hopes for (d_i = f(book_lev, roe)*g(x)) is a smooth product of two chars, and the pipeline audit measured the RFF basis as 87% inside the 21-dim quadratic span of the same chars -- so DKKM's marginal advantage over an FM that gets both chars linearly is bounded by the quadratic-minus-linear gap, which was measured at 0.871 -> 0.909 of max SR^2, i.e. +2.2% in Sharpe. That is the same ~1.03x DKKM/FM the baseline already produces.
verdicts.salvage: Split into two deliverables. (1) MANDATORY PREREQUISITE, no economics, no defense needed: reconcile the sigma_x/sigma_z exponents (2/3 vs 3/2), the risk-free rate (0.1/12 vs 0.074830/12), the tax placement, and xi vs GS21_ZETA (0.03 vs 0.01) between GS21.m and config.py; then verify GS21.m reproduces the shipped solfiles bit-for-bit before touching anything else; and add an explicit off-grid counter to replace the silent fill_value=None extrapolation. Nothing in this repo is interpretable until this is done. (2) SEPARATE, DEFENDED CALIBRATION CHANGE: restore sigma_z to the paper's 0.0956 (removing the 2026-06-09 ad hoc 0.1 factor is a repair; it is the model's own documented value), and treat rho_z = 0.985 as an optional robustness variant rather than the baseline, so the grid cost is a choice rather than a requirement.

verdicts.proposal_name: Permanent cross-sectional heterogeneity in asset risk: J discrete industry types with different sigma_z
verdicts.critique:
The economics is the most defensible in the set -- a single common sigma_z across all firms is genuinely GS21's least attractive homogeneity assumption, industry cash-flow volatility heterogeneity is well measured, the solve is separable by type, and the SDF and internal consistency are untouched. I have no structural objection. My objection is that the quantitative premise is wrong, and it is wrong in a way that makes the proposal nearly inert.

GS21'S IDIOSYNCRATIC RETURN VARIANCE IS NOT DRIVEN BY z. It is ~95% the investment lottery. panel_functions_gs21.py:141 defines rets = k[1:]*P[1:]/(k[:-1]*P_ex[:-1]) - 1, and k jumps by the factor g = 1.14 with probability cutoff/imax. From the shipped i_cut_down, mean cutoff = 39.57 against imax = 2000, so p = 0.0198 and the Bernoulli capital jump contributes variance p(1-p)(g-1)^2 = 3.80e-4, i.e. a return sd of 1.95%/month. The prior diagnosis measured GS21's total idiosyncratic sd at 1.54-2.67%/month. The z channel contributes (dlogP/dz)*sigma_z = 0.32*0.014034 = 0.45%/month, variance 2.0e-5 -- about 5% of the idiosyncratic variance. The eta lottery contributes sqrt(zeta(1-zeta))*(G/P) = 0.05%/month, essentially nothing.

So a 5x permanent spread in sigma_z moves per-firm idiosyncratic return sd from roughly 1.95% to roughly 1.99% at the high type and 1.94% at the low type. The proposal's headline prediction -- 'idio-volatility cross-sectional range 1.7x -> ~5x, sd(log idio variance) from ~0.25 to ~0.75' -- is off by an order of magnitude, because it implicitly assumes idiosyncratic variance is proportional to sigma_z^2 when in this model it is nearly independent of sigma_z. The proposal is only rescued if it is stacked on top of Proposal 3's FULL 10x sigma_z restoration, in which case the z channel becomes 9.4e-4 and dominates -- but then the proposal is a rider on a change the proposer ranked as an 'enabler,' and the combined package is no longer minimal.

SECOND PROBLEM, which the proposal half-concedes: the D^{-1} channel is worth O(1/N) absent an unspanned premium. The theory agent's own oracle-span experiment found the inverse-variance tilt worth 0.186% of max Sharpe at N=1000 even with a 20x spread in d, and that adding extreme heteroskedastic D to an exact-factor-pricing economy moved the RFF-over-linear ceiling from 1.00 to 0.999. GS21 IS an exact-factor-pricing economy: mu is by construction minus the conditional covariance with Mmat, and Mmat is a one-shock exogenous lognormal (GS21.m:138). So heteroskedastic D in GS21 is a multiplier on an alpha that does not exist.

THIRD: permanent, never-changing types are a fixed effect. With a 360-month rolling window and a noiseless-enough cfvol proxy, FM learns the type almost perfectly. The proposal's own escape -- 'the whole DKKM edge rests on the proxy being NOISY and the optimal map being a nonlinear shrinkage' -- is a claim about the ESTIMATOR (that unpenalized OLS cannot represent E[1/sigma | proxy]), not about the model, and the correct response to it is to give FM a ridge penalty, not to change the economics. A referee will say exactly that.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: FM captures nearly all of it, and the proposal supplies the refuting numbers itself: linear R^2 of exp(-c*u) is 0.861 at a 25x variance range and 0.763 at 100x, with quadratic R^2 of 0.991 and 0.971. So a monotone inverse-variance tilt in one char hands FM 76-86% and hands a quadratic 97-99%. The residual for a 3600-feature basis is a few percent of a channel that is itself worth O(1/N) of max Sharpe. The one genuinely non-linear piece -- the ratio book_lev/b*(cfvol) -- is dead on arrival at the current solution quality: b_refin_0 takes only THREE distinct values over the entire 80,000-point grid ({0.2105, 0.2632, 0.3158}), because bnum = 20 quantizes the refinancing target to a 0.053 grid. There is no resolvable distance-to-target for a ratio to be formed from. And the claimed FF handicap (value weighting excludes the high-idio-vol tail) is not economics in this model: mve = k*P_ex and k is a Bernoulli random walk with no reset (zero defaults), so sd(log k) grows as sqrt(T) and 'size' is a burn-in artifact rather than a steady-state object.
verdicts.salvage: Two redirections, both cheaper and both hitting the channel that actually controls D in this model. (a) Put the permanent type heterogeneity in the INVESTMENT technology rather than in sigma_z: firm-specific g and imax (equivalently, lumpiness and frequency of investment spikes). This is what drives 95% of idiosyncratic variance here, it is disciplined by Cooper-Haltiwanger plant-level spike rates, and crucially p(1-p)(g-1)^2 is NON-MONOTONE in the investment cutoff -- it peaks at p = 0.5 -- so idiosyncratic variance becomes a genuinely non-monotone, interactive function of (z, x, b) rather than the monotone function FM eats. That is the ratio nonlinearity H2 needs, and it costs one parameter. (b) If permanent types are wanted, put them in phi (recovery rate / asset tangibility, GS21.m line 32) rather than sigma_z: tangibility is a canonical measured characteristic, it enters the default payoff MULTIPLICATIVELY with b, it changes b* materially rather than by 0.008, and it becomes live the moment default becomes reachable. Either way, replace 'permanent' with a slow Markov migration so the type is not a learnable fixed effect.

verdicts.proposal_name: Turn on the equity-issuance kink kappa_e and widen the debt grid so the negative-cash-flow region and the default boundary are reachable
verdicts.critique:
The internal-consistency finding here is correct, important, and under-sold. GS21.m DOES contain a live i.i.d. valuation shock nu ~ N(0, sigma_m^2 = 25) inside the default decision: line 204 evaluates the debt payoff with the indicator ((P_up_old + nodes') > 0) and line 263 computes the equity value as sum(max(P_up_old + nodes', 0).*weights), i.e. E_nu[max(P+nu, 0)]. The simulation at panel_functions_gs21.py:72 tests default[t] = (P[t] <= 0) with no shock at all, and sdf_compute_gs21.py's integ_zi_zj_x has no default branch. So the shipped value function prices a default option that the simulation and the 'true' conditional moments both assume away. At the grid corner where P_down = 4.73 (the global minimum I verified over all 80,000 points) the solve assigns Phi(-4.73/5) = 17% monthly default probability while the simulation assigns zero. That is a genuine defect and it should be fixed regardless of whether anyone wants more nonlinearity.

BUT THE PROPOSED LEVERS ARE THE WRONG ONES, in a specific way.

(1) bmax IS NOT THE BINDING CONSTRAINT AND RAISING IT IS UNJUSTIFIED. The proposal's premise -- borrowed from the diagnosis's 'GS21 firms are effectively all-equity, max 1% market leverage' -- is an artifact of the broken mkt_lev characteristic (Proposal 2). I computed the correct object from the solfiles: at the center of the state space, Q_0/(Q_0+P_down) = 0.330 at b = 0.316, and b_refin_0 = 0.316. GS21's firms carry 33% market leverage, which is ON the calibration target, and interest/EBITDA = (1-tau)*0.316/1.0 = 0.30, i.e. coverage 3.4x -- a healthy investment-grade firm, not a firm pinned at a grid ceiling. There is no evidence the b grid binds; b* sits at 32% of bmax. Widening bmax to 1.5-2 solves a problem the model does not have, and it costs a re-solve plus (per the proposal) a cut of znum from 200 to 100, degrading the z resolution that Proposal 3 needs to WIDEN.

(2) THE kappa_e KINK IS NOT MERELY HARD TO REACH, IT IS UNREACHABLE BY 22 STANDARD DEVIATIONS. Profit is nonpositive when exp(x+z) <= delta + (1-tau)*b. At b = b* = 0.316 that requires x+z <= log(0.00667 + 0.0667*... ) = -1.199. The joint stationary sd of x+z under the SOLVE process is sqrt(0.038431^2 + 0.036707^2) = 0.0531, so the kink sits at -22.6 sd. Under config's (mismatched) process it is -15.6 sd. Raising tau to 0.20 raises b* and helps a little; raising bmax to 1 brings the threshold to -0.062, still -1.2 sd, but firms never choose b = 1. So the kappa_e channel is strictly conditional on Proposal 3's full sigma_z restoration, which raises sd(z) to 0.554 and puts the kink at roughly -2.2 sd. The proposal says this in its risk section; it should say it in its title. As written it would be shipped, produce literally zero change, and cost a full re-solve.

(3) DEFAULT IS ALSO A sigma_z PROBLEM, NOT A bmax PROBLEM. Equity is worth ~190 per unit capital against a coupon of 0.316; default requires the entire perpetual profit stream to become worthless. In Gomes-Schmid's own paper default is driven by persistent idiosyncratic productivity declines. Restore sigma_z and default becomes reachable; widen bmax and it does not.

(4) THE sigma_m PROPOSAL IS UNDER-SPECIFIED IN A DANGEROUS WAY. Adding nu ~ N(0,25) to the simulated price at P ~ 190 injects a 2.6%/month i.i.d., UNPRICED, non-state return shock -- comparable to the entire measured idiosyncratic volatility. That would flood D with pure noise and, since sdf_compute_gs21.py's ERR does not model nu, would make the 'true' cond_var wrong by more than it is now. If nu is turned on in the simulation it MUST be turned on in the conditional second moment simultaneously, and the paper must be explicit that it is a numerical smoothing device with no economic content -- an awkward thing to have carrying a nonlinearity result.

IDENTITY: unlike Proposals 1, 4 and 6, this one turns on frictions the model already declares (GS21.m lines 33, 253-254, 259-260 for kappa_e; lines 53-59, 204, 263 for sigma_m). That is the least ad hoc move in the set and the paper's 'simple economic models' claim survives it cleanly.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: Conditional on Proposal 3, the default channel is the only mechanism in this list that could plausibly reach real-data magnitudes, because it is the only one that generates order-of-magnitude idiosyncratic-variance dispersion and a genuine left tail. But the proposal's own analysis concedes the decisive point: the default-probability channel is convex but MONOTONE in distance-to-default, and it measured linear R^2 = 0.763 even at a 100x range. FM, handed a distance-to-default characteristic (which Proposal 2 supplies), gets three-quarters of it, and a quadratic gets 97%. The two arguments left -- that a threshold in the tail is less linear than one at the median (R^2 0.27 vs 0.75), and that the kink location moves with x_t -- are real but small, and the second one is partly available to FM, which is re-estimated monthly and can shift an intercept. The FF-value-weighting argument I discount entirely: with zero defaults k is a Bernoulli random walk, so 'small' is a burn-in artifact, and once defaults exist the reset k = 0.2*mean(k) makes small firms mechanically young rather than economically distressed. Realistic expectation: a DKKM/FM gap of 1.2-1.4x, not the claimed 1.3-1.6x standalone or 2.5-4x combined.
verdicts.salvage: Reorder and shrink. Ship in this sequence: (i) the mandatory mismatch repairs from Proposal 3; (ii) sigma_z restored to the paper value -- this alone is what makes both the kappa_e kink and the default boundary reachable, and it requires no change to bmax, kappa_e or sigma_m; (iii) THEN check reachability empirically on the re-solved grid (is P_down < 0 anywhere the simulation visits? does prof <= 0 occur at b*?) before spending anything on bmax or kappa_e. Turn on kappa_e = 0.025 (GS21.m's own commented value, not 0.05) only if step (iii) shows the region is visited. Turn on nu in the simulation ONLY together with the matching (1 - Phi(-P'/sigma_m)) survival factor in sdf_compute_gs21.py's payoff and the correct Bernoulli-mixture second moment on the diagonal, and be prepared to defend it as a smoothing device. Fix the two latent bugs first: panel_functions_gs21.py:85 fails to write the redrawn xt back into x[t], and the while loop at line 73 has no iteration cap.

verdicts.proposal_name: A genuinely independent second priced aggregate shock: a credit-conditions state s_t with its own price of risk
verdicts.critique:
This inherits both of Proposal 1's fatal errors and adds a 64 GB re-solve on top.

(1) SAME 20x AMPLITUDE ERROR. The proposal writes beta_s = (P_up - P_down)/P_ex and then computes the premium as sd(G/P)*theta_s*gamma_s = 0.00241*0.46*0.101 = 1.1e-4, claiming 17% of the cross-sectional premium. That uses the same undiscounted theta_s = 0.46. Correctly, the return's exposure to a 1-sd s innovation is (dV/dzeta)*(zeta*theta_s*sqrt(1-rho_s^2))*avg(rho_s^h)/P = 35*(G/P)*0.01*0.46*0.183*0.63 = 0.019*(G/P), so the premium contribution is gamma_s*0.019*(G/P), with cross-sectional sd = 0.101*0.019*0.00241 = 4.6e-6, against an existing premium sd of 6.7e-4. That is 0.7%, not 17% -- and it is 0.005% of the VARIANCE of expected returns. The proposal's own conclusion that this must be combined with a 3x amplitude recalibration to reach 33%, and with Proposals 3 and 5 to reach 80%, is therefore itself off by ~20x: even the full stack lands at a few percent.

(2) SAME FALSE V-SHAPE. The 'why FF/FM cannot' section rests entirely on beta_s being 'a symmetric quadratic in (book_lev - b*)' with 'exactly zero covariance with the characteristic.' I measured G/P from the shipped solfiles: over the visited support b in [0, 0.32] it is monotone decreasing with linear R^2 = 0.930 mean, 0.988 median, and the minimum value -0.00197 equals exactly -kappa_b*Q_0/P_down, which proves eta=1 is a FORCED costly refinancing rather than an option and that the envelope-theorem vertex does not exist. FM spans this. FF's high-minus-low leverage sort captures it. The claimed structural blindness of the linear methods is simply not a property of this model.

(3) THE HEDGING ARGUMENT ALSO FAILS. The proposal's second-order claim -- that linear methods 'lose twice' because they cannot hedge beta_s -- requires beta_s to be outside the linear char span. At linear R^2 = 0.93 it is inside it.

(4) IDENTITY AND INTERNAL CONSISTENCY, THE HARSHEST PART. GS21 is an equilibrium model in which the SDF is the marginal rate of substitution of a representative Epstein-Zin agent over aggregate consumption driven by x. Bolting on an orthogonal priced state s means the agent's marginal utility jumps for reasons with no consumption counterpart -- that is an intermediary SDF (He-Krishnamurthy), a different model with a different marginal investor. The proposal's defense is that GS21.m's beta = 0.994, varphi = 2, gamma = 10 at lines 14-16 are 'NEVER USED' and the SDF is already an exogenous lognormal with gamma_x = 0.5, so gamma_s is no more free than gamma_x. I verified this is true (Mmat at line 138 is exp(-r - 0.5*gamma_x^2 - gamma_x*eps_x') with no reference to the preference parameters). But that is an argument for FIXING the SDF, not for adding a second free parameter to a kernel that is already disconnected from the stated agent. Note also that gamma_x = 0.5 implies a maximal monthly Sharpe of sqrt(exp(0.25)-1) = 0.533, i.e. 1.85 annualized -- roughly 3-4x the empirical market Sharpe. The model's headline aggregate calibration target is ALREADY missed by a factor of three. Adding a second free price of risk to that is rigging, and a referee will name it as such.

(5) COST. The proposal concedes the dense Mmat goes to 64 GB and that tauchen.m is absent and no MATLAB is installed. It is proposing the most expensive item in the set to buy a channel I have shown to be ~0.7% of the premium dispersion and 93% linear.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: No, on three grounds, any one of which is sufficient. First, magnitude: the correctly computed credit premium is 0.7% of the existing cross-sectional premium sd, so mu stays numerically rank-1 no matter what the algebraic rank is. Second, shape: the new loading is 93-99% linear in book_lev on the visited support, so FM spans it and FF's leverage sort gets it -- the proposal's whole DKKM-specific argument evaporates. Third, and most damning, the diagnosis's own numbers already refute the premise that a second shock is what is missing: BGN and KP14 BOTH have two aggregate shocks and both produce DKKM/FF ratios of 1.04 or negative. Rank-2 is not the threshold; DKKM's own Theorem 3 criterion is an effective rank of E[FF'] in the hundreds, and going from 1 to 2 priced shocks moves the measured effective rank of 16-21 by essentially nothing. The proposal would spend weeks of re-solve to move the priced-risk dimension from 1 to 2 in a theory that needs tens.
verdicts.salvage: Abandon the credit-supply framing. The defensible way to get a second priced direction into GS21 costs nothing in free parameters and is already sitting unused in the source: ACTIVATE THE EPSTEIN-ZIN PARAMETERS AT GS21.m LINES 14-16. Derive Mmat from beta = 0.994, varphi = 2, gamma = 10 over an aggregate consumption process driven by x, and add stochastic volatility to x. Then (i) the SDF becomes the marginal rate of substitution of the stated agent, repairing a real internal-consistency violation; (ii) the price of x-risk becomes state-dependent rather than a free 0.5 that overshoots the market Sharpe by 3-4x, repairing a real calibration violation; (iii) you get a genuine SECOND priced factor -- volatility risk -- whose price is PINNED by gamma and varphi rather than chosen to manufacture a result; and (iv) the vol-risk loading is a duration/convexity object that depends on leverage NONLINEARLY, which is the shape difference the proposal wanted and did not get from zeta. It costs one grid dimension, the same as s, but it is Bansal-Yaron plus Gomes-Schmid rather than He-Krishnamurthy grafted onto Gomes-Schmid, and no referee can call it rigging.

missed_ideas: PREREQUISITE, NOT A PROPOSAL -- the shipped value function solves a DIFFERENT stochastic process than the simulation. Verified exactly: zgrid.max() = 0.146826069677159 equals 4 stationary sd of sigma_z = 0.1*0.16*sqrt((1-0.9^(2/3))/(1-0.9^2)) = 0.0095599, and xgrid.max() = 0.153723027652884 equals 4 stationary sd of sigma_x = 0.012*sqrt((1-0.95^(2/3))/(1-0.95^2)) = 0.0070463 -- the GS21.m (2/3) exponents. config.py:286,289 use the (3/2) exponent, giving 1.484x and 1.468x larger shocks. So P_up/P_down/i_cut/b_refin are not optimal policies for the simulated economy, the state runs off-grid into silent linear extrapolation (fill_value=None at sdf_compute_gs21.py:61-74), and -- decisively -- the rp/cond_var/max_sr that every method is scored against are not the true moments of any internally consistent model. No GS21 result is interpretable until GS21.m is shown to reproduce the shipped solfiles. Proposal 3 mentions this inside its 'exact change' block; it belongs at the top of the whole document.

THE RISK-FREE RATE IS INCONSISTENT BETWEEN THE KERNEL AND THE EXCESS RETURN. GS21.m:27 sets r = 0.1/12 = 0.0083333 inside Mmat (line 138), so the value function discounts at 10%/yr. config.py:299 sets GS21_R = 0.074830/12 = 0.0062358, used at panel_functions_gs21.py:296 (df.ret -= exp(r)-1) and at sdf_compute_gs21.py's ER[0,0] = exp(2r) and ER[0,1:] = (eret+1)*exp(r). Every 'true' conditional risk premium therefore carries a spurious +0.21%/month = +2.5%/yr level. Against a measured cross-sectional MEAN rp of 0.35-1.33%/month this is a large share of the level, and the market leg of max_sr is correspondingly an artifact. Cheap to fix, and it changes the headline numbers.

THE TAX BASE DIFFERS BETWEEN SOLVE AND SIMULATION. GS21.m:124 sets pi_Rmat = (exp(x+z) - delta) - (1-tau)*b, taxing only the interest deduction. panel_functions_gs21.py:113-118 uses (1-tau)*exp(x+z) - delta - (1-tau)*b, taxing operating profit as well. Since P_ex = P - Ecashflow (line 129), the simulated ex-dividend price is internally inconsistent with the value function by tau*exp(x+z) ~ 0.067 per unit capital, shifting every expected return by ~3.5e-4/month = 0.42%/yr.

THE REFINANCING RATE ITSELF IS INCONSISTENT. GS21.m:35 sets xi = 0.03/3*3 = 0.03; config.py:296 sets GS21_ZETA = 0.03/3 = 0.01. The solve used a refinancing arrival rate 3x the one the simulation (panel_functions_gs21.py:49) and the conditional-moment code (sdf_compute_gs21.py:132, 177, 184; panel_functions_gs21.py:200-201) use. Both Proposal 1 and Proposal 6 are built entirely on making zeta state-dependent; neither can be evaluated until the constant is reconciled.

eta=1 IS A FORCED, COSTLY REFINANCING -- NOT AN OPTION. GS21.m:253 sets prof0_up = pi_Rmat + ((1-kappa_b)*Q_0(b') - Q_0(b)), so a firm already at b* still pays kappa_b*Q_0. I verified the consequence in the solfiles: G/P = (P_up-P_down)/P_down is NEGATIVE for b in [0.26, 0.37], with minimum -0.00197 = -kappa_b*Q_0/P_down exactly. There is no envelope-theorem vertex and no symmetric V. Moreover on the visited support b in [0, 0.32] G/P is monotone DECREASING and 93-99% linear in b (linear R^2 mean 0.930, median 0.988 across 400 (z,x) slices). This single fact kills the 'why FF/FM cannot' argument of both Proposals 1 and 6. It is also worth reporting as an economic limitation: in this implementation the refinancing 'opportunity' is a tax, not an option.

THE REFINANCING TARGET IS QUANTIZED TO THREE VALUES. b_refin_0.csv and b_refin_I.csv each take exactly three distinct values over all 80,000 grid points: {0.2105, 0.2632, 0.3158}, because bnum = 20 gives a b-spacing of 0.0526 and b_refin is bgrid(argmax). Any mechanism keyed on |b - b*| -- Proposals 1, 4 and 6 all are -- is unresolvable at this grid. bnum must rise substantially before distance-to-target means anything, and that is a cost none of them budgeted.

GS21'S IDIOSYNCRATIC RETURN VARIANCE IS ~95% THE INVESTMENT LOTTERY, NOT PRODUCTIVITY. rets = k[1:]*P[1:]/(k[:-1]*P_ex[:-1]) - 1 (panel_functions_gs21.py:141) and k jumps by g = 1.14 with probability cutoff/imax. From i_cut_down.csv, mean cutoff = 39.57 against imax = 2000, so p = 0.0198 and p(1-p)(g-1)^2 = 3.80e-4, i.e. a return sd of 1.95%/month -- essentially the whole measured idiosyncratic sd of 1.54-2.67%. The z channel gives (0.32*0.014034)^2 = 2.0e-5, about 5%; the eta lottery gives 0.05%/month. This reframes the whole D-heterogeneity discussion, invalidates Proposal 4's quantitative premise, and identifies the real lever: idiosyncratic variance in GS21 is p(1-p)(g-1)^2 where p = i_cut(z,x,b)/imax. That is ALREADY characteristic-linked and, critically, NON-MONOTONE in the cutoff (it peaks at p = 0.5), which is exactly the shape H2 needs and that a monotone heteroskedasticity channel cannot supply. Retargeting imax and g jointly against Cooper-Haltiwanger investment-spike moments (spike rate ~8%/yr, spike size ~20%) is a one-parameter, well-disciplined change that no proposal considered.

THE VARIANCE OF THE REALIZED INVESTMENT COST IS DELETED FROM THE CONDITIONAL SECOND MOMENT, AND THE AUTHOR CLEARLY INTENDED IT TO BE THERE. sdf_compute_gs21.py's live diagonal is P_0_sq = (1-prob_i)*(P_up_0^2*zeta + P_down_0^2*(1-zeta)) and P_I_sq = prob_i*(P_up_I^2*zeta + P_down_I^2*(1-zeta)); the commented-out block immediately above it contains the full version with the cash-flow terms and the term prob_i*(imin^2 + imin*i_cutoff + i_cutoff^2)/3 -- the second moment of the uniform investment-cost draw. Turning that back on adds a Bernoulli x Uniform idiosyncratic risk source that is a genuinely non-Gaussian, non-monotone function of the cutoff, i.e. of (z, x, b). It requires no new economics, no re-solve, and no free parameter -- the model already assumes i_cost ~ U[imin, imax]. This is the cheapest live D-channel in the model and nobody proposed it.

ACTIVATE THE EPSTEIN-ZIN PARAMETERS THAT ARE ALREADY DECLARED AND UNUSED. GS21.m lines 14-16 set beta = 0.994, varphi = 2, gamma = 10, and they appear nowhere else in the file; the SDF at line 138 is an exogenous lognormal Mmat = exp(-r - 0.5*gamma_x^2 - gamma_x*eps_x') with a free gamma_x = 0.5. Two consequences nobody drew. First, the model as implemented has NO stated agent, so 'is the SDF still the marginal rate of substitution?' is already answered no -- which weakens the identity objection to Proposal 6 but strengthens the objection that the paper's 'simple economic models' framing oversells what is being simulated. Second, gamma_x = 0.5 implies a maximal MONTHLY Sharpe of sqrt(exp(0.25)-1) = 0.533, i.e. 1.85 annualized -- 3-4x the empirical market Sharpe, so GS21's headline aggregate calibration target is already missed by a factor of three. Deriving Mmat from the declared EZ preferences over an x-driven consumption process, with stochastic volatility in x, would simultaneously (a) repair the internal-consistency violation, (b) repair the equity-premium/Sharpe calibration, and (c) deliver a SECOND priced factor whose price of risk is pinned by gamma and varphi rather than chosen -- and whose loading is a duration/convexity object that depends on leverage nonlinearly. This dominates Proposal 6 on every dimension including cost.

PERMANENT HETEROGENEITY IN phi (RECOVERY RATE / ASSET TANGIBILITY) IS A STRICTLY BETTER TYPE DIMENSION THAN sigma_z. GS21.m:32 sets phi = 0.4 as a scalar and it enters the default payoff at line 128 as def_Rmat_pre = phi*(1 - delta + exp(x+z)). Tangibility/redeployability is a canonical, well-measured firm characteristic (Almeida-Campello, Berger-Ofek), it enters MULTIPLICATIVELY with the default state so it interacts with leverage rather than adding to it, it shifts b* materially (unlike sigma_z, which moves b* by 0.008), and it becomes the dominant cross-sectional risk determinant the moment default is reachable. Same per-type re-solve cost as Proposal 4, far more interaction content, and no change to the shock structure.

THE FIRM-SIZE DISTRIBUTION IS NON-STATIONARY, SO 'SIZE' IS A BURN-IN ARTIFACT AND EVERY VALUE-WEIGHTING ARGUMENT IS SUSPECT. With zero defaults, k[t+1] = (1 + invest*(g-1))*k[t] is a pure Bernoulli random walk with no reset, so sd(log k) grows as sqrt(T) and never converges. Several proposals lean on 'FF value-weights so it misses the distressed small-cap tail' (Proposals 4 and 5) -- but in this model 'small' means 'unlucky in the investment lottery during burn-in,' not 'economically distressed.' Any DKKM advantage that runs through the size distribution is an advantage over a non-economic artifact. Fixing this needs either a live default/reset process or decreasing returns / a size-dependent investment technology, neither of which any proposal supplies.

NO PROPOSAL ADDRESSES THE FACT THAT THE INVESTMENT TECHNOLOGY HAS NO CURVATURE. Capital grows by a fixed factor g = 1.14 or not at all; there is no adjustment-cost curvature, no q-theory, no decreasing returns to scale, and no dependence of the growth option on z or on size. That is why agr has exactly two values and why the cross-section of investment carries no information. Making the growth increment depend on z or on the state (a genuine growth-option, Kogan-Papanikolaou style) would generate a real investment characteristic, a stationary size distribution, and a second source of char-dependent risk -- and it is squarely inside the production-based tradition rather than grafted from a different literature.

THE COMPARISON'S LINEAR BENCHMARK IS HANDICAPPED AND EVERY 'FM CANNOT DO THIS' ARGUMENT INHERITS THE HANDICAP. fama_functions.fama_macbeth regresses on RAW, unstandardized characteristics via pinvh with the standardization block commented out, mixing log-size of order 5 with bm of order 1. Any GS21 result reported as 'DKKM beats FM' is partly reporting 'DKKM beats a badly conditioned FM.' Fix FM's conditioning and give it the same ridge grid DKKM gets BEFORE claiming any span advantage; otherwise the referee's first question -- 'is the linear benchmark being handled competently?' -- has an embarrassing answer.

REPORT max_sr AND Sharpe/SR* BEFORE PROPOSING ANY MODEL CHANGE. max_sr is computed at sdf_compute_gs21.py:222-224 and stored in every *_moments.pkl but never propagated into results.pkl by evaluate_sdfs.py. Since the Sharpe metric is exactly SR*_t * cos_Sigma(w, w*_t), the interpretable number is the cosine. If FF already attains 0.86 of SR* -- as the population span calculation says it does -- then no estimator change and no marginal model change can produce a 3-5x gap, and the whole exercise should be reframed rather than patched. This is a one-line change and it should gate every proposal in this document.
